title: Germany news: Conservative state premiers rally behind Merz
summary: All eight CDU state premiers have backed Friedrich Merz, urging the party to focus on rebuilding trust. Plus, Germany's coalition is weighing rapid relief as record fuel prices pile pressure on…

image.caption: Hendrik Wüst (left) is among the eight CDU state premiers who have jointly backed Merz, but is also touted as a possible successor (FILE: 01/09/2025)Image: Malte Ossowski/Sven Simon/IMAGO

blocks.text: All eight CDU state premiers have backed Friedrich Merz, urging the party to focus on rebuilding trust. Plus, Germany's coalition is weighing rapid relief as record fuel prices pile pressure on households. DW has more.

blocks.caption: Hendrik Wüst (left) is among the eight CDU state premiers who have jointly backed Merz, but is also touted as a possible successor (FILE: 01/09/2025)Image: Malte Ossowski/Sven Simon/IMAGO

items: All eight Christian Democratic Union (CDU) state premiers have publicly backed Chancellor Friedrich Merz amid growing unease over his leadership
The premiers said the party should focus on rebuilding trust rather than debating whether to replace Merz
Germany's coalition is considering rapid relief as petrol and diesel prices climb to record or near-record levels
The center-right CDU is pushing tax cuts, while the center-left Social Democratic Party favors a price cap

Bavaria's Söder lends weight to Merz amid CDU turmoil

blocks.caption: Söder has backed Merz and called for an end to the leadership debate (FILE: 02/07/2026)Image: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has also thrown his support behind Chancellor Friedrich Merz, adding his voice to those of eight CDU state leaders backing the chancellor amid growing pressure over his leadership.
Söder leads the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU), the CDU's sister party in Bavaria. The two parties together form the CDU/CSU conservative bloc at the national level.
Söder explicitly backed Merz on Tuesday and called on the CDU to end its internal debate over the chancellor's future.
